questions.question: What is phishing?
questions.explanation: Phishing emails pretend to be trusted senders to steal passwords or install malware.

questions.question: Got a suspicious email. What should you do?
questions.explanation: Report it with the phishing button or to IT; never click links or open attachments.

questions.question: MFA adds what to your password?
questions.explanation: Multi-Factor Authentication adds a code or app approval, blocking most stolen-password logins.

questions.question: A strong password should be?
questions.explanation: Long passphrases unique to each account are hard to guess or crack.

questions.question: Found a USB drive in the parking lot?
questions.explanation: Unknown USB drives may carry malware; hand them to IT without plugging them in.

questions.question: What does ransomware do to files?
questions.explanation: Ransomware encrypts data and demands payment; backups and patching are the defence.

questions.question: Shortcut to lock a Windows PC?
questions.explanation: Windows + L locks the PC instantly, protecting data when you step away.

questions.question: Letting someone follow you through a secure door?
questions.explanation: Tailgating bypasses access control; everyone must badge in themselves.

questions.question: Sharing your login with a colleague is?
questions.explanation: Accounts are personal; every action under your ID is traced to you.

questions.question: India's national cyber incident agency?
questions.explanation: CERT-In is India's national agency for responding to cyber security incidents.

questions.question: CERT-In incident reporting deadline?
questions.explanation: CERT-In's 2022 directions require reporting specified cyber incidents within 6 hours.

questions.question: Information security management ISO?
questions.explanation: ISO 27001 defines requirements for an Information Security Management System.

questions.question: Auto industry info-security assessment?
questions.explanation: TISAX is the automotive industry's information security assessment for suppliers.

questions.question: Social engineering attacks mainly target?
questions.explanation: Attackers trick people into giving access, so awareness is the first line of defence.

questions.question: Working on public Wi-Fi needs a?
questions.explanation: A VPN encrypts traffic so data cannot be read on untrusted networks.

questions.question: In ERP, what does 'R' stand for?
questions.explanation: Enterprise Resource Planning links finance, purchasing, production and sales in one system.

questions.question: SAP module for purchasing and stores?
questions.explanation: Materials Management handles purchase orders, goods receipt and inventory.

questions.question: SAP module for sales orders and billing?
questions.explanation: Sales & Distribution covers sales orders, deliveries and invoices.

questions.question: SAP module for production orders?
questions.explanation: Production Planning manages BOMs, routings, MRP and production orders.

questions.question: SAP module for financial accounting?
questions.explanation: Financial Accounting records ledgers, payables, receivables and statements.

questions.question: SAP PM module handles what?
questions.explanation: Plant Maintenance manages breakdown and preventive work orders for machines.

questions.question: Example of a master data error?
questions.explanation: A wrong unit or price in material master data causes errors in every later transaction.

questions.question: BOM stands for?
questions.explanation: A BOM lists all parts and quantities needed to make one finished item.

questions.question: MES connects ERP to the?
questions.explanation: A Manufacturing Execution System tracks real-time production, quality and traceability.

questions.question: Controller that runs factory machines?
questions.explanation: A Programmable Logic Controller runs machine sequences, sensors and actuators on the line.

questions.question: Secure standard linking machines to MES?
questions.explanation: OPC UA is a secure, vendor-neutral standard for industrial machine data exchange.

questions.question: OT (vs IT) mainly controls what?
questions.explanation: Operational Technology runs physical processes and needs separate security zones from IT.

questions.question: Barcodes on part boxes help with?
questions.explanation: Scanning labels links each lot to its process, materials and inspection records.

questions.question: IIoT sensors on machines help to?
questions.explanation: Connected sensors stream vibration and temperature data to spot problems early.

questions.question: The HMI screen on a machine is used to?
questions.explanation: The Human-Machine Interface lets operators view status and control equipment.

questions.question: What protects PCs during power cuts?
questions.explanation: An Uninterruptible Power Supply gives battery backup for safe shutdown.

questions.question: Before installing software at work?
questions.explanation: Unapproved software can carry malware or break licence terms.

questions.question: 3-2-1 backup rule: offsite copies?
questions.explanation: Keep 3 copies on 2 media types with 1 copy offsite or offline for recovery.

questions.question: A firewall's job is to?
questions.explanation: Firewalls allow or block network traffic based on security rules.

questions.question: Software patches mainly fix what?
questions.explanation: Patches close vulnerabilities that attackers exploit, so install them promptly.

questions.question: RTO in disaster recovery means?
questions.explanation: Recovery Time Objective is how fast systems must be restored after an outage.

questions.question: RPO in disaster recovery means?
questions.explanation: Recovery Point Objective is how much recent data (in time) the business can afford to lose.

questions.question: Example of cloud SaaS?
questions.explanation: Software as a Service runs in the cloud and is used through a browser or app.

questions.question: RAID 1 means what?
questions.explanation: RAID 1 writes the same data to two disks, so one can fail without data loss.

questions.question: DNS converts what?
questions.explanation: The Domain Name System translates names like nsk.com into IP addresses.

questions.question: A clean desk policy means?
questions.explanation: Lock away documents and devices so confidential information isn't exposed.

questions.question: India's personal data law of 2023?
questions.explanation: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 governs personal data in India.

questions.question: Send confidential drawings to vendors via?
questions.explanation: Approved, encrypted file sharing with access control protects design IP.

questions.question: Who owns data on company laptops?
questions.explanation: Company devices and data belong to the company and follow IT policy.

questions.question: Usual label for engineering drawings?
questions.explanation: Engineering drawings are intellectual property and usually classified confidential.

questions.question: Emailing data to the wrong person is?
questions.explanation: Misdirected emails with sensitive data must be reported to IT/security quickly.

questions.question: Best way to log an IT issue?
questions.explanation: Tickets record the issue, priority and fix, so nothing gets lost.

questions.question: First step when your PC freezes?
questions.explanation: A simple restart fixes many issues; raise a ticket if the problem repeats.

questions.question: Keyboard shortcut to copy?
questions.explanation: Ctrl+C copies, Ctrl+V pastes, Ctrl+X cuts and Ctrl+Z undoes.

questions.question: 'Shadow IT' means using?
questions.explanation: Tools not approved by IT create hidden security and data risks.
